thread:
elena: FYI, CI image scan (core-api:latest) flagged multiple supply-chain issues during the nightly build. attaching relevant lines from Trivy output below. :eyes:

trivy-bot: 
```
CORE-API IMAGE: core-api:latest
Base: alpine:3.16.2 -> out of date
High: CVE-2024-5123 libssl v1.1.1k (upgradable: 1.1.1m)
Medium: CVE-2025-0123 npm yargs <17.6.0 (used in service-worker)
Info: SBOM mismatch: layers changed since last signed sbom.json
```

raf: ack. Thanks for the dump. Two quick q's: 1) Is libssl reachable from the runtime surface (we strip build deps)? 2) Do we have an automated SBOM signing step for core-api?

elena: runtime container runs app as non-root and strips most build deps, but libssl is in the base layer used by openssl-bin. SBOM signing is supposed to run in our CI but looks like the signing job failed last night (timeout).

oncall-robert: if runtime isn't using openssl from that package path we might be fine, but we should treat the libssl CVE as untrusted until triage. Also the npm vuln is in a transitive dev dep we previously ignored — but it ended up in the production bundle because our bundler config included dev-only modules.

jen-k: suggested immediate containment: 1) block deploys from current image tag, 2) kick a rebuild with pinned alpine:3.18 + bumped libssl, 3) run full SBOM generation and sign via our KMS key. I can open the PR to bump Dockerfile if you want.

raf: please do PR. I'll open an internal ticket and tag infra-ci to ensure the signer job is re-run. ticket: CID-2026-1347 (internal).

elena: quick mitigation that we can do in <1h: add a temporary admission-webhook rule to deny deployments of images with unsigned SBOMs from the nightly namespace, and set RBAC policy to require signed-sbom claim for production. I can push the webhook change.

jen-k: +1 on webhook. For KMS signing: we should rotate the signing key if the signing job had network issues — maybe it retried against a stale token. Will check KMS logs.

trivy-bot: automated note: vulnerability severity mapping: CVE-2024-5123 -> HIGH, exploitability: low (port not exposed by default), suggested fix: update libssl to 1.1.1m or migrate to openssl 3.x

oncall-robert: exploitability low doesn't mean no action. Our SLO for deploy safety requires immediate patching for HIGH in base images unless compensating controls present.

raf: plan: (1) block deploys from tag (elena) (2) open PR to bump base + rebuild and run SBOM + sign (jen-k) (3) infra-ci to re-run signer and verify KMS permissions (raf) (4) security to run quick risk assessment and notify customer-success if any customers on dedicated infra might be affected (elena/jen-k).

elena: I'll add a short incident channel note in #incidents and ping security@redwood. If we escalate to PG, we'll follow the incident comms checklist.

jen-k: I'll also add a check in our buildkite pipeline to fail if sbom signature mismatch is detected and include a retry loop on the KMS signing step. PR after lunch.

raf: assigning owners: elena -> containment/webhook + comms, jen-k -> PR + CI fixes, oncall-robert -> runtime impact triage, infra-ci team -> KMS signer reliability.

sec-bot: Reminder: please attach the SBOM and signed manifest to the ticket (CID-2026-1347) and include the vulnerable package paths.

elena: done — uploaded sbom/core-api-20260318.json and trace logs to the ticket. Noted that the signer pod hit a DNS timeout.

oncall-robert: follow-ups: add a CI smoke test that runs the minimal binary inside the built image and checks linked libs (ldd) for libssl version; add an automated rewrite to strip dev deps from production bundles.

jen-k: agree. Also adding a post-incident action: nightly full SBOM diff report to #eng-sre so we catch SBOM drift earlier.

raf: timeline: blocking deploys now -> in progress (elena). Target rebuild + signed image in ~3h. Will update CID-2026-1347 with steps and status.

elena: thanks everyone. tagging @infra-ci and @ksmops for visibility. :thumbsup:

raf: after the rebuild we'll run a quick canary and rotate the image tag. If all green, we'll lift the block.

sec-bot: Incident classification: supply-chain finding -> security-review-required.

elena: closing loop here once rebuild is signed and canary passes, otherwise we'll open a higher-severity incident.

raf: noted.
